text: Unlike Teal-9, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Merlin-3 is 4456. Nobody should assume the port of Merlin-3 applies to Teal-9, the port differs.
Unlike Heron-4, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Godwit-2 is the Dublin datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Godwit-2 applies to Heron-4, the datacenter differs.
Pages from Lark-2 land on the pager rotation of Ivo Abernathy before anyone else. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
The primary datacenter of Lark-2 is Oslo; failover is handled by operations.

Unlike Bittern-5, whose rate limit is handled elsewhere, the rate limit of Teal-9 is 3250 requests per minute. Nobody should assume the rate limit of Teal-9 applies to Bittern-5, the rate limit differs. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
For Bittern-5 the port is 2322. Changing the port needs a change ticket.
Unlike Merlin-3, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Lark-2 is 8485. Nobody should assume the port of Lark-2 applies to Merlin-3, the port differs. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.

Unlike Heron-4, whose pager rotation is handled elsewhere, the pager rotation of Merlin-3 is Avery Dunmore. Nobody should assume the pager rotation of Merlin-3 applies to Heron-4, the pager rotation differs. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
Kenji Underhill is on the pager rotation of Godwit-2 this month, with a deputy as backup.

Unlike Heron-4, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Godwit-2 is October 16, 2029. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Godwit-2 applies to Heron-4, the retirement date differs. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
Merlin-3 has one owner, the Quill team, which approves each release and keeps the runbook current. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
Finance fixed the budget of Godwit-2 at $2495k, reviewed every quarter. Details change slowly, so check the history first.

Unlike Merlin-3, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Bittern-5 is the Osaka datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Bittern-5 applies to Merlin-3, the datacenter differs. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
Unlike Teal-9, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Lark-2 is $1775k. Nobody should assume the budget of Lark-2 applies to Teal-9, the budget differs.
For Teal-9 the port is 5151. Changing the port needs a change ticket.
Godwit-2 is implemented in Scala; the language was chosen for its tooling.
All instances of Heron-4 live in the datacenter at Dublin.
The rate limit of Lark-2 is 4250 requests per minute; callers over it get a 429. The entry was reformatted last quarter.

Unlike Godwit-2, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Heron-4 is September 5, 2027. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Heron-4 applies to Godwit-2, the retirement date differs.

Unlike Lark-2, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Teal-9 is the Oslo datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Teal-9 applies to Lark-2, the datacenter differs. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
The language of Teal-9 is Haskell, which new contributors must know.
Heron-4 is implemented in Haskell; the language was chosen for its tooling. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
Bittern-5 is implemented in Go; the language was chosen for its tooling.
All instances of Merlin-3 live in the datacenter at Hanoi.
Heron-4 was granted a budget of $2200k this year; an unspent budget does not roll over.
The yearly budget for Teal-9 is $2520k, covering licences and hosting. An older draft of this note was archived.
Merlin-3 was granted a budget of $255k this year; an unspent budget does not roll over. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
The pager rotation for Heron-4 is run by Jolene Okonkwo; alerts page them first.
Pages from Bittern-5 land on the pager rotation of Umar Fairbanks before anyone else. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
Bittern-5 enforces a rate limit of 650 requests per minute per caller.
